MYRP Project Description & Scope

May-26-Dec-28 The Breaker Replacement project involves replacing degraded transmission and 

distribution class circuit breakers, including oil circuit breakers (“OCBs”), with 
modern circuit breakers that utilize gas and vacuum-based technologies. 

2

3

4

5

6

7

T02

Capacity & Customer 
Planning

Distribution Plant in Service, 
Transmission Plant in Service

Apr-26-Dec-28

T03

Line H&R

Transmission Plant in Service

Jan-27-Dec-28

T04

Sub H&R

Distribution Plant in Service, 
Transmission Plant in Service

May-26-Dec-28

The Transmission System is required to meet NERC Standards and reliably serve 
customers. NERC and local standards set requirements for transmission system 
power flows, voltages, stability, and breaker capability to maintain a safe and 
reliable transmission grid and avoid widespread grid blackouts. Project scope 
includes upgrading equipment such as line conductors, transformers, breakers, 
and switches to a higher capacity. Protective relay systems are upgraded to add 
redundancy to help reduce the likelihood and severity of critical equipment 
outages.

The Transmission Line H&R project includes cathodic protection, targeted line 
strengthening for extreme weather, and wood pole replacement.

The Transmission Substation H&R project includes the replacement of major 
substation assets along with ancillary equipment. This project can include the 
following major assets and ancillary equipment:  Transformers, Breakers, Circuit 
Switchers, Regulators, Protective Relays, Instrument Transformers, Disconnect 
Switches, Capacitor Banks, Wooden & Lattice Structures that support the electrical 
bus, and Arrestors.  Scope may also include animal mitigation and physical 
security.

T05

System Intelligence

Distribution Plant in Service, 
Transmission Plant in Service

May-26-Dec-28 The System Intelligence Project provides grid operators and engineers with 

enhanced information to more rapidly respond to changing conditions that 
challenge reliability. This project falls within the following three scopes: Relays 
Upgrades, Remote Substation and Asset Monitoring, and Enabling Remote 
Controlled Switches.

T06

Transformers

Distribution Plant in Service, 
Transmission Plant in Service

Apr-26-Dec-28

The Transformer Bank Replacement project replaces degraded transmission 
transformers.

T07

Vegetation 
Management

Transmission Plant in Service

Jan-27-Dec-28

The Transmission Integrated Vegetation Management (IVM) Danger Tree Project 
focuses on the removal of trees outside of the right of way identified as hazards to 
minimize the risk of vegetation-related outages.

Reason for the MYRP Project
This project will improve fault interrupting capabilities and 
support modernizing communication and control 
functionalities which better positions the electric grid to 
effectively respond to grid events for the benefit of 
customers and the environment.  These highly reliable gas 
and vacuum breakers are also better suited for protecting 
circuits with higher solar and other variable energy resource 
penetration. 

As demand on the transmission system grows and changes 
over time, new transmission projects are needed to keep the 
grid reliable for customers and in compliance with NERC 
Standards.  DEC is also required to connect new 
transmission delivery points for retail and wholesale 
customers.

The Transmission Line Hardening & Resiliency (H&R) 
project creates a stronger and more resilient transmission 
grid capable of withstanding or quickly recovering from 
severe weather and other extreme external events which 
lead to  structural degradation, affecting the performance of 
the transmission system.  

The Transmission Substation Hardening & Resiliency (H&R) 
project not only enhances the functionality of individual 
assets, but improves the overall functionality of the system, 
particularly under extreme weather conditions.

The System Intelligence project provides enhancements that 
support critical information necessary to respond to 
changing conditions that threaten reliability. Relay Upgrades 
modernize relays to improve protections to the transmission 
system and equipment and allow quicker recovery from 
system events and service disruptions. Remote Substation 
and Asset Monitoring allows proactive decisions to be made 
when equipment health is threatened. Enabling Remote 
Controlled Switches play a vital role in sectionalizing 
transmission lines to limit the customer impact of faults from 
external causes and equipment failures.

The  Transformer Replacement Project anticipates future 
transmission class transformer failures and replaces those 
transformers in a proactive manner with modern 
transformers avoiding customer outages, collateral damage, 
and oil release requiring environmental mitigation. 

The Transmission Vegetation Management Danger Tree 
Project minimizes vegetation-related interruptions while also 
maintaining compliance with regulatory, environmental, and 
safety requirements and standards to support the safe and 
reliable operation of the transmission system.

Duke Energy Carolinas, LLC Docket No. E-7, Sub 1329Fogg Direct Exhibit 5 Page 1 of 20Project Purpose 

The  Transmission  Breaker  Replacement  project  proactively  replaces  degraded  substation  circuit  breakers, 
including  oil  circuit  breakers,  with  modern  circuit  breakers  that  utilize  advanced  gas  and  vacuum-based 
technologies. This project enhances grid reliability by reducing customer outages associated with the failure of 
legacy equipment. 

Individual Project Details 

Individual  project  details  including  locations,  costs,  and  timelines  for  construction  and  in-service  dates  are 
included in Fogg Direct Exhibit 4.   

Project Description 

The  key  scope  of  the  Transmission  Breaker  Replacement  project  encompasses  the  replacement  of  both 
transmission  class  (44kV  and  above)  and  distribution  class  (below  44kV)  circuit  breakers  located  within 
transmission substations.  Circuit breakers serve a critical role in substations by remotely or locally connecting 
or  disconnecting  transmission  or  distribution  circuits  and  rapidly  interrupting  fault  currents  to  prevent 
widespread outages. 

The project involves replacing degraded circuit breakers that currently use mineral oil as the insulating medium, 
now  considered  a  legacy  technology.  These  existing  oil  circuit  breakers  are  at  or  near  the  end  of  their 
operational life and face challenges such as lack of spare parts and manufacturer support. The breakers are 
replaced with modern gas and vacuum circuit breakers. These new breakers improve fault interruption speed 
and  reduce  environmental  risks  linked  to  oil  spills.  Upgrading  to  newer  technologies  ensures  continued 
operational  performance  and  efficiency,  which  is  especially  important  as  circuits  increasingly  support  grid 
expansion. 

 Transmission Oil Circuit Breaker  

    Transmission Gas Circuit Breaker

Circuit  breakers  play  a  vital  role  in  isolating  system  disturbances.    The  Transmission  Breaker  Replacement 
project  strategically  replaces  degraded  and  outdated  oil  circuit  breakers  with  circuit  breakers  that  utilize 
modern gas and vacuum technologies. This approach enhances grid capabilities by improving fault interrupting 
performance, increases system resiliency through rapid outage recovery, enables additional system capacity, 
and reduces the environmental footprint.

Project Purpose 

The  Transmission  Capacity  and  Customer  Planning  project  ensures  the  transmission  system  complies  with 
North American Electric Reliability Corporation (“NERC”) Standards to support reliably serving customers. This 
involves meeting requirements for power flows, voltages, stability, and breaker capabilities to maintain grid 
safety and prevent widespread blackouts. 

Individual Project Details 

Individual  project  details  including  locations,  costs,  and  timelines  for  construction  and  in-service  dates  are 
included in Fogg Direct Exhibit 4. 

Project Description 

The Transmission Capacity and Customer Planning project scope includes upgrading transmission equipment 
such  as  line  conductors,  transformers,  breakers,  and  switches  to  higher  capacities.  Transmission  Planning 
performs studies to identify future overloads and develops a plan to optimally address the overloads through 
system upgrades, which may include non-traditional solutions such as energy storage.  

The  project  scope  also  includes  enhancing  protective  relay  systems  with  redundancy  to  help  reduce  the 
likelihood and severity of critical equipment outages. The recent version 5.1 of NERC Standard TPL-001 added 
additional  requirements  for  redundancy  of  protection  systems  which  are  detailed  in  Footnote  13  (FN13)  of 
Table  1  of  the  Standard.  Transmission  owners  must  bring  their  systems  into  compliance  with  the  updated 
redundant protection requirements by July 1, 2029. In addition to meeting NERC standards, the FN13 projects 
will improve the reliability of the transmission grid by ensuring that protection systems operate as planned, 
even under single element failure. 

Overall,  these  transmission  upgrades  help  maintain  grid  reliability  and  compliance  with  NERC  Standards  as 
customer demand grows.

Project Purpose 

The Transmission Line Hardening & Resiliency (“Line H&R”) project replaces and strengthens transmission line 
structures and associated assets to create a stronger, more resilient, and reliable transmission grid capable of 
withstanding extreme external events and rapidly recovering from disruptions. 

Individual Project Details 

Individual  project  details  including  locations,  costs,  and  timelines  for  construction  and  in-service  dates  are 
included in Fogg Direct Exhibit 4. 

Project Description 

Key scopes of the Transmission Line H&R project include implementation of cathodic protection, line rebuilds, 
static/overhead ground wire replacements, and wood pole replacements. Each scope of work is discussed in 
more detail below.   

Cathodic  Protection:  Installation  of  magnesium  anodes  on  transmission  towers  to  mitigate  corrosion  and 
extend their lifespan. Towers that are identified as corroded to the point of impacting structural integrity are 
addressed through installation of structural braces, or through complete tower replacement when warranted. 

Line Rebuilds: Replacement of vulnerable wooden structures and lattice steel towers, upgrading 44kV and 66kV 
lines to support reliability and future capacity, including renewable energy integration. These rebuilds can also 
include switch, conductor, and static wire replacements. 

Static Wire/Overhead Ground Wire (“OHGW”): Replacement of degraded static wires to support protection 
against lightning, with some replacements including upgrade to fiber optic ground wire that provide high-speed 
communication capabilities between substations. 

Wood Pole Replacement: Replacement of degraded wood poles with durable non-wood alternatives such as 
steel, concrete, or ductile iron to reduce risk of unplanned outages caused by pole failures and extend service 
life. 

Implementation of these Transmission Line H&R scopes significantly improves the transmission grid's ability to 
withstand  extreme  weather,  maintain  service  continuity  for  customers,  and  reduce  recovery  time  from 
disruptions.

Project Purpose 

The Transmission Substation Hardening & Resiliency (“Sub H&R”) project replaces major assets and ancillary 
equipment inside transmission substations to create a stronger and more resilient transmission grid capable of 
withstanding extreme external events and rapidly recovering from disruptions. 

Individual Project Details 

Individual  project  details  including  locations,  costs,  and  timelines  for  construction  and  in-service  dates  are 
included in Fogg Direct Exhibit 4. 

Project Description 

The  key  scopes  of  the  Transmission  Sub  H&R  project  include  comprehensive  reliability  upgrades  and 
implementation of substation animal mitigation.  Each scope of work is discussed in more detail below.   

Substation Reliability Upgrades: This scope includes the replacement of major substation assets, along with 
ancillary equipment, to improve reliability by reducing the risk of unplanned outages due to equipment failure.  
These upgrades are planned, designed, and executed for cost efficiency, often incorporating multiple assets.   
In some cases, the scope encompasses entire substation rebuilds.  Additionally, when necessary to minimize 
outage impacts to customers, temporary mobile equipment is utilized during the construction phase of this 
project.  

The scopes may include one or all of the following major assets and ancillary equipment:1 

•  Transformer(s) 
•  Breaker(s) 
•  Circuit Switcher(s) 
•  Regulator(s) 
•  Protective Relay(s) 
• 
•  Disconnect Switches 
•  Capacitor Banks 
•  Wooden & Lattice Structures that support the electrical bus 
•  Arresters 

Instrument Transformers (CCVT, PT, CT) 

Animal  Mitigation  (Vanquish  Fence):  Installation  of  specialized  fencing  to  prevent  animal  interference  on 
substation equipment that can lead to sustained customer outages or momentary voltage depressions.

Project Purpose 

The  System  Intelligence  project  modernizes  protective  relays  and  implements  advanced  monitoring 
technologies  to  provide  enhanced  information  that  supports  rapid  response  to  conditions  that  threaten 
electrical grid reliability.  

Individual Project Details 

Individual  project  details  including  locations,  costs,  and  timelines  for  construction  and  in-service  dates  are 
included in Fogg Direct Exhibit 4. 

Project Description 

Key scopes of the System Intelligence project include relay upgrades, enhancing remote substation and asset 
monitoring, and enabling remote controlled switches. Each scope of work is discussed in more detail below: 

Relay Upgrades: Replacement of outdated electromechanical and solid-state relays with digital relays. Digital 
relays offer enhanced communication capabilities, microprocessor technology, and multifunctionality, allowing 
for  quicker  recovery  from  system  events.  They  also  enable  features  such  as  fault  location  identification, 
reducing time for manual line patrols during troubleshooting following an event. Additionally, as part of the 
relay upgrade scope, communication-assisted protection equipment that is obsolete or no longer meets design 
specifications is replaced to mitigate the risk of device mis-operations.

control of substations by system operators. The scope also includes installation of condition-based monitoring 
(“CBM”)  equipment  to  continuously  monitor  critical  transformer  conditions  to  predict  asset  health  and 
remaining life expectancy, allowing for proactive decisions when asset health is threatened.

Project Purpose 

The Transmission Transformer Replacement project proactively replaces degraded transmission transformers 
to enhance grid reliability by reducing customer outages and environmental risks associated with unexpected 
transformer failures. 

Individual Project Details 

Individual  project  details  including  locations,  costs,  and  timelines  for  construction  and  in-service  dates  are 
included in Fogg Direct Exhibit 4. 

Project Description 

The key scope of the Transmission Transformer project encompasses the replacement of transformers located 
within transmission substations. The scope of work is discussed in more detail below: 

Transformer  Replacements:  The  health  of  substation  transformers  is  monitored  through  a  predictive 
maintenance program. Diagnostic tests, such as electrical testing and dissolved gas analysis (DGA) of insulating 
oil, are routinely conducted as part of the program. These tests diagnose potential issues like abnormal heating 
and moisture presence. The resulting data is fed into the Health and Risk Management (HRM) platform, which 
uses machine learning to assess transformer health and inform timely replacement decisions. Transformers 
showing signs of deterioration may undergo additional monitoring or testing and, if necessary, are selected for 
planned, condition-based replacement. This project includes the following types of transformer replacements: 
•  Transmission-to-Transmission (T/T) – High-voltage and low-voltage windings operate at 44kV or higher 

(e.g., 500kV/230kV). 

•  Transmission-to-Distribution  (T/D)  –  High-voltage  winding  operates  at  44kV  or  higher;  Low-voltage 

winding operates at 35kV or lower (e.g., 100kV/13kV). 

•  Distribution-to-Distribution  (D/D)  -  High-voltage  winding  operates  at  35kV  or  lower;  Low-voltage 

winding operates at 12.5kV or lower (e.g., 24kV/12.5kV).  

                                T/T Transformer                                                                            T/D Transformer

Project Purpose 

The  Transmission  Vegetation  Management  Danger  Tree  project  enhances  the  transmission  grid  so  that  it  is 
capable of withstanding extreme weather events and reduces the frequency of outages impacting customers.      

Individual Project Details 

Individual  project  details  including  locations,  costs,  and  timelines  for  construction  and  in-service  dates  are 
included in Fogg Direct Exhibit 4. 

Project Description 

The danger tree project within the Transmission Integrated Vegetation Management (“IVM”) Program focuses 
on ensuring the reliable operation of the transmission system by minimizing vegetation-related interruptions 
and maintaining adequate conductor-to-vegetation clearances, while maintaining compliance with regulatory, 
environmental, and safety requirements or standards. A danger tree is a tree that is dead, diseased, dying or 
leaning towards a line, or any tree that could, due to its proximity, shape, type, or size, otherwise endanger 
Company assets. Project activities focus on the removal of vegetation along the right-of-way to minimize the 
risk of vegetation-related outages, and to ensure necessary access within all transmission line corridors.  

A multi-year vegetation work plan based on the date of previous work, outage history, and line criticality serve 
as  the  core  work  strategy.  This  plan  is  then  optimized  by  a  threat-based  and  condition-based  approach, 
incorporating intelligence obtained through remote sensing, inspections, and field assessments.

Is the Project Required by Law? 

Yes. Select work under this project is required to maintain compliance with the applicable NERC Standards in 
FAC-003. 

Explanation of Need for Proposed Expenditure 

Transmission outages from vegetation can be extremely disruptive to customers and costly for the Company. 
Additionally,  vegetation-caused outages can also create regulatory compliance issues for the Company.  The 
Transmission  Vegetation  Management  Danger  Tree  project  works  to  create  a  hardened  transmission  grid 
capable of minimizing the impacts of extreme weather events and reducing the frequency of outages impacting 
customers.

Financial cost-benefit analyses methodology

T R A N S M I S S I O N

Overall methodology

• Benefits calculation and cost-benefits analysis completed using methodology from previous rate cases

• Expected financial benefits based primarily on outage risk reduction

• Cost-benefit analyses completed for individual project locations

Data inputs

Methodology for benefits and costs

Copperleaf cost-benefit analyses 

• Cost Estimate based on historical

project data (i.e., average requirements
for completion of work, materials)

• Total Project costs including costs

outside of the MYRP2 project in-service
window

• Asset Condition based on field

assessments, inspections (probability of
failure for end-of-life assets)

• Risk of Overload based on system
planning studies and analysis (for
capacity projects)

• Consequence of Failure based on
voltage level, circuit configuration,
customer mix

• Project benefits calculated based on

outage risk reduction

o Financial value of outage risk

reduction (reliability improvements)
calculated using Interruption Cost
Estimate (ICE) Calculator

• Timing of costs and benefits determined

from expected project schedules

• Third party software used to assess

project benefits

• Annual avoided outage benefits

assessed for 30-year life following
project in-service

• Net present value and benefit-cost ratio

calculated for each project location
